= TCK compatibility check

CI runs the unchanged official TCK at revision
`cdfada9c2768b164eadf4bc12e9f9c68e6caf68a`. It uses Node 25.8.2, the version
selected by that checkout. The adapter still reports 11 passing cases and two
failures. The CI check accepts only these two known incompatibilities:

* `block/listing/multiple-lines`: strict export rejects the listing's unnumbered
  caption state. The diagnostic must match completely, including its kind, path
  and source range. The command must fail without writing partial JSON.
* `block/section/title-body`: export retains the real generated `_section_title`
  ID. Its complete graph must equal the upstream expectation with only that ID
  added. No other property or source location may differ.

The check does not change the adapter, parser, export policy or upstream files.
It verifies the checkout revision and clean state, all 13 cases, the official
failure counts and diagnostics, and both complete adapter responses. A new or
changed failure, skipped case or unexpected pass fails CI and needs review.
A green job means the known compatibility boundary is unchanged; it does not
mean that all TCK cases pass or that acdc fully conforms to AsciiDoc.

Run it from the repository root after installing the pinned TCK dependencies:

[source,console]
----
cargo build -p acdc-cli --no-default-features --features tck
node --test .github/tck/check.test.mjs
node .github/tck/check.mjs ../asciidoc-tck target/debug/acdc
----

The self-tests check that extra output differences, changed diagnostics and
unexpected test outcomes fail the gate. When changing the TCK pin, review these
cases and the check together. Keep upstream expectations unchanged.
